title: Thin-slot shield leakage estimate
description: Estimate the worst-orientation field leakage through one electrically small, thin rectangular slot. Engineering estimate, not enclosure compliance.
assumptions: One isolated slot in an otherwise highly conducting shield; L>w and L>=10t define the thin-slot geometry used here.
L<=lambda/20 restricts operation to the manufacturer's electrically small design guideline.
Worst polarization/orientation estimate; no cavity resonance, seams, multiple apertures, penetrations or near-field magnetic shielding.
Estimate only, not a certified shielding effectiveness or EMC compliance result.

references.title: Laird technical note 154, Rule-of-Thumb for Calculating Aperture Size, page 1

constraints.message: The longest dimension must exceed the width; this is a slot, not a round aperture.
Thin-slot estimate requires length at least ten times shield thickness.
Slot length must not exceed wavelength/20 for this screening model.

title: RC input-filter common-mode conversion
description: Predict differential interference created by mismatched RC input legs, including the bridging differential capacitor. Engineering estimate, not immunity compliance.
formula: D=R2 C2-R1 C1; a=1-w^2 R1 R2[C1 C2+Cd(C1+C2)]; b=w[R1(C1+Cd)+R2(C2+Cd)]; |Vdiff/Vcm|=w|D|/hypot(a,b)
assumptions: Both ideal source nodes carry the same sinusoidal RMS common-mode voltage relative to the capacitor return.
R1 and R2 feed separate high-impedance receiver inputs; C1 and C2 shunt these nodes to the common return; Cd bridges the receiver nodes.
Lumped linear ideal components; effective source resistances may be included in R1/R2. No receiver loading, rectification, capacitor voltage dependence or amplifier CMRR.
Differential polarity is node one minus node two. Output voltage is a nonnegative RMS magnitude.
Estimate only, not proof of RF immunity or EMC compliance.

references.title: Texas Instruments, Art Kay, Common mode and differential filter, 2022, pages 2-5

outputs.label: Signed RC mismatch R2C2 minus R1C1

title: Trapezoidal conducted-current harmonic
description: Estimate one conducted harmonic from a symmetric-edge switching-current pulse train and its known resistive termination voltage. Not a receiver compliance reading.
formula: fn=n fs; Idc=Ipk D; In,rms=sqrt(2) Ipk |sin(pi n D)/(pi n)| |sin(pi n fs tr)/(pi n fs tr)|; Vn,rms=R In,rms
assumptions: Periodic unipolar trapezoid has equal linear 0-to-100% rise and fall times tr, not oscilloscope 10-to-90% times.
D is pulse width between the half-amplitude crossings divided by period. tr<=min(D,1-D)/fs prevents overlapping edges.
Input current is the actual current delivered to a purely resistive RF termination, not an unfiltered switch current assumed to reach a LISN.
No frequency modulation, ringing, nonlinear load, spectral detector, resolution bandwidth or LISN transfer model is included.
Harmonic RMS amplitude estimate only; never a peak/quasi-peak compliance prediction. Analytic harmonic nulls may leave floating-point sine residuals.

references.title: Texas Instruments, Rice/Gehrke/Segal, Understanding Noise-Spreading Techniques, section IV equation 1 and Figure 2

inputs.label: Equal full rise and fall time

constraints.message: Harmonic order must be a positive integer.
Full rise and fall edges must fit the high and low intervals.
The positive edge-to-period argument must be representable.

title: Switching-frequency dither harmonic occupancy
description: Use Carson's sinusoidal-FM estimate to plan harmonic spreading and adjacent-harmonic overlap. Does not predict an EMC detector's reduction.
assumptions: Instantaneous switching frequency is fs+Deltaf sin(2 pi fm t); Deltaf is peak deviation, not peak-to-peak.
An otherwise fixed periodic waveform is phase/frequency modulated sinusoidally; its nth harmonic has deviation n Deltaf.
Carson bandwidth is an approximate occupied band containing roughly 98% of single-tone FM power, not a hard spectral boundary.
Negative adjacent-band gap means the estimated occupied bands overlap. Real sidebands extend outside both bands.
No flat-spectrum assumption, dB reduction, resolution-bandwidth weighting, converter stability or compliance claim is made.

references.title: Texas Instruments, Rice/Gehrke/Segal, Understanding Noise-Spreading Techniques, section IX and Figure 7

outputs.label: Signed gap to next Carson band

constraints.message: Peak deviation must remain below nominal frequency so switching never reverses or stops.
This switching-dither interpretation requires modulation slower than the carrier.
Harmonic order must be a positive integer.
